summary: Iteration 6 verified NEW passwordless email magic-link sign-in ALONGSIDE the existing Emergent Google login, and re-ran full regression of iterations 1-5. Backend: 70 pytest tests / 70 passed (0 failed) in ~24s (xdist -n 2). Added /app/backend/tests/test_magic_link.py [8 tests]: (1) POST /api/auth/magic/request with RESEND_API_KEY empty returns 503 with detail 'Email sign-in is not configured yet. Add a RESEND_API_KEY.'; (2) invalid EmailStr body → 422; (3) missing email field → 422; (4) POST /api/auth/magic/verify with bogus token → 400 'invalid or already used'; (5) HAPPY PATH — seeded magic_links doc {token_hash=sha256(raw).hex, used:false, expires_at=+15min}; verify returns user + sets session_token cookie + creates user_sessions row + marks magic_links.used=true; second call with same token → 400 (single-use enforced); (6) EXPIRED — seeded doc with expires_at in the past → 400 'expired'; (7) MERGE-BY-EMAIL (critical) — pre-inserted user {user_id:'existing_uid_<ts>', email:jane@…} + owned session + settings doc + prior user_sessions token; seeded magic_links for SAME email; verify returned user_id == existing_uid (no duplicate user row created), and GET /api/sessions with the NEW session_token lists Jane's prior session id (shared data confirmed); (8) response body contains no mongo _id. Regression (unchanged from iter 5, all still green): test_auth_gating.py [25] — all protected endpoints 401 without token, /api/ public 200, /api/auth/session 401 on invalid session_id, /api/auth/logout public 200, valid Bearer+cookie both work; test_isolation.py [10] — A/B cross-tenant isolation + per-user settings/keys; test_providers.py [~15] — provider routing, no raw keys in responses, graceful 400/502 without keys; backend_test.py — CRUD, message/synth/tts length caps 422, STT 415 non-audio + 200 audio, PDF export application/pdf %PDF magic, review 'two members must speak' 400, rate-limit burst → 429 with 'rate limit' detail. Frontend: /login shows BOTH google-login-btn AND magic-email-input + magic-link-btn as expected. Submitting an email calls POST /api/auth/magic/request and (after rate-limit window reset) receives 503; the UI shows a red toast 'Email sign-in is not configured yet. Add a RESEND_API_KEY.' and does NOT switch to the magic-sent state; page does not crash and the form is still usable. Unauthenticated GET / redirects to /login. Note: earlier the frontend call returned 429 because backend rate-limit bucket was still saturated from the immediately-preceding pytest burst test — this is expected behaviour (magic/request is under the 60/min rate limit) and the UI degraded gracefully with a 'Rate limit exceeded' toast (no crash). After the 65s window the 503 path was verified as described.
critical_code_review_comments: magic/verify auto-creates a NEW user if the email has never signed in before (via _login_user). This is by design ('accounts merge by email') but effectively means anyone with access to the mailbox can create an account — that's fine for a magic-link flow, but note there is NO email-domain allowlist and no captcha on /auth/magic/request, so someone knowing the pattern could burn through the 60/min rate-limit to spam any inbox once RESEND_API_KEY is configured. Consider a per-email cooldown (e.g. 1 request per email per 60s) in addition to per-IP.

magic_links docs are never garbage-collected — 'used' and 'expired' rows accumulate forever. Add a TTL index: db.magic_links.createIndex({expires_at:1},{expireAfterSeconds: 3600}) (with expires_at stored as a BSON Date, not ISO string) so Mongo auto-purges. Same recommendation stands from iter 5 for user_sessions.expires_at.

In magic_request the origin used to construct the sign-in link is taken from request.headers['origin']; if a client sends a spoofed Origin, the emailed link could redirect a victim to attacker.tld/login#magic=<token>. The token is single-use and 15-min, but the token would still be leaked to the wrong origin. Consider pinning to APP_BASE_URL env, or validating origin against an allowlist.

MagicRequest uses EmailStr but does NOT lowercase before hashing; magic_verify likewise doesn't lowercase the email stored back into users via _login_user (though _login_user matches by exact email string). So a user requesting 'Jane@X.com' will land in a different users row than one who Google-signed-in as 'jane@x.com'. server.py:370 does email.strip().lower() for the magic_links doc, and _login_user is called with doc['email'] (lowercased) — so magic-side is fine, but the Google callback (/auth/session) uses the Emergent-provided email verbatim. If Google returns mixed case, the merge-by-email guarantee could silently break. Suggest normalising email to lower() inside _login_user itself.
resend.api_key is set at module import time from RESEND_API_KEY; changing the env at runtime won't take effect until backend restart. Not a bug, but worth documenting.

The 503 detail string is user-facing ('Add a RESEND_API_KEY') which is technically an implementation leak — end users don't know what a RESEND_API_KEY is. Consider softening to 'Email sign-in is temporarily unavailable' for prod.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (login page shows both methods; 503 gracefully handled; unauth redirect verified)

test_credentials: Same pattern as iter 5 — seed users/user_sessions directly via pymongo (see /app/backend/tests/conftest.py) and use Authorization: Bearer <session_token>. For magic-link tests: seed /magic_links doc with token_hash=sha256(raw).hexdigest() and future expires_at ISO; verify by POSTing the RAW token. RESEND_API_KEY is empty in /app/backend/.env (503 path is what's exercised); EMERGENT_LLM_KEY present.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral. test_magic_link.py uses a per-test cleanup_tracker fixture that records inserted user_ids, magic_links token_hashes, session ids, and settings _ids, then delete_many by exact id/hash in teardown. Post-run mongo state: 0 residual test users, 0 residual magic_links, 0 residual test sessions. No broad regex used (per iter-5 lesson about xdist worker races).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Total 70 pytest tests pass (~24s, xdist -n 2). To add magic-link cases: hash token = hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest(); insert into db.magic_links {email (lowercased), token_hash, used:false, expires_at:iso, created_at:iso}; POST /api/auth/magic/verify {token: RAW}. When invoking magic/request from playwright, be aware /api/auth/magic/request is under the shared 60/min per-IP rate limit — if pytest just ran the burst test, wait ~65s or the frontend will see 429 not 503. Frontend renders the toast via sonner; the visible text is the API's detail string. AuthContext parses BOTH #session_id (Google) and #magic=<token> (magic-link) on bootstrap. Do NOT restore any broad-regex cleanup in conftest — races between xdist workers.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. During frontend testing the first attempt hit 429 instead of 503 because the pytest suite's rate-limit-burst regression test had just filled the 60/min bucket for this IP; after waiting 65s the 503 path was cleanly verified. This is not a bug — the rate limiter is deliberately shared across magic/request and the expensive endpoints.
